subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser-specific URL/domain/path denylist or warnlist, or fold this into a broader egress/security policy instead?
rationale: This would become public operator-trusted browser navigation policy and new config surface, and the related open issues show competing browser-only, private-network, and cross-tool scopes that automation should not choose.

options.title: Design browser policy first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser deny/warn behavior for navigation, redirects, proxy-routed profiles, default lists, errors, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold into generic egress policy
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39685 the canonical direction if maintainers want one allow/deny policy across browser, web_fetch, web_search, and plugin HTTP egress.

options.title: Reject core denylist surface
options.body: Close this direction if maintainers decide bot-blocked public domains should remain an operator workflow outside OpenClaw config, while documenting current hostname allowlist/private-network controls.

recommendation.title: Design browser policy first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser deny/warn behavior for navigation, redirects, proxy-routed profiles, default lists, errors, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on browser SSRF defaults, navigation guard policy, and the published security docs this decision would extend.
